description: Rules of the reality show The Traitors (UK format, also used in the US and Australia), one season per seed. Show name and rules only; no footage, logos or real contestants.
rules_source: Wikipedia, The Traitors (British TV series), sections Format and End Game, read 13.11.2026

assumptions.herd: Chance a Faithful who has no read follows the current vote leader.
assumptions.p_shield: Chance a shield is won on a given day (missions vary).
assumptions.p_accept: Chance a recruited Faithful accepts (most do on the show).
assumptions.end_doubt: Chance each Faithful votes 'banish again' at each End Game fire.
assumptions.faithful_model: v0.2 'suspicion': each Faithful scores every other player and votes for the top score.
assumptions.d: How much more suspicious a real Traitor looks than an innocent player, in units of noise. 0 = pure guessing. Calibrated, not observed.
assumptions.rho: Share of a Faithful's private noise that is a fixed hunch for the whole season (the rest changes daily).
assumptions.shared: Share of suspicion that all Faithful hold in common on a given day (the mood of the room).

calibrated_block.label: Real-player read, Traitors vote as a fixed block

calibrated_herd.label: Real-player read, Faithful follow the leader half the time

calibration.target: Traitors won 6 of 10 finished seasons with a winner (US 1-4, UK 1-4, Australia 1 and 3; Australia 2 had no winner), Wikipedia 13.11.2026
calibration.note: d solved by bisection on 4,000 seasons per step with rho 0.5 and shared 0.5; Wilson 95% for 6/10 is 31-83% Traitor wins, i.e. d 0.28-0.78

method: One season of The Traitors per seed under the show's published rules; player behaviour knobs are the author's assumptions (see rules.json). Exact counts; 95% Wilson intervals measure sampling only.
